info.name: Keycloak ACR Step-up POC
info.description:
Passkey/password step-up POC (Keycloak 26.4). OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE, PUBLIC clients (no secret).

Run a request: Authorization tab > **Get New Access Token** > log in as **alice / alice** > **Use Token** > **Send**. The `acr`/`amr` claims are NOT in the userinfo body — they live in the token, so after Send open the **Visualize** tab (and the Postman Console) to see them decoded. The raw token is saved to the `accessToken` collection variable.

The ACR path is baked into each request's Auth URL. This collection uses "Authorize using browser" (your system browser), which supports real passkeys — so the default passkey path can complete there too. Ensure https://oauth.pstmn.io/v1/callback is allowed (it is, on these clients).

item.name: Exact client (postman)
item.description: Custom exact-match flow: default = passkey only, loa/low = password only.

exec: // Decode the Bearer access token Postman injected, log + visualize acr/amr.

'(Collection → Variables). Open the Visualize tab to see this.

';
pm.visualizer.set(tpl, { acr: c.acr, amr: JSON.stringify(c.amr), azp: c.azp, user: c.preferred_username });
console.log('No JWT bearer yet — click "Get New Access Token", Use Token, then Send.');

request.description:
No acr_values at all -> the client's default.acr.values (=…/loa/x509) applies, so this is the DEFAULT login method: X.509 client certificate over mutual TLS (:8443), no password fallback.

Same prereqs as the explicit X.509 request: 'Authorize using browser' ON, and import certs/alice.p12 (password 'changeit') into your OS keychain / browser cert store so the system browser presents alice's cert. Result: acr=…/loa/x509, amr=["x509"] (Visualize tab). With no certificate the login is refused.

request.description: Identity-first passkey (acr_values=…/loa/high). Enter the username: passkey holders log in with their passkey (amr=hwk); passkey-less users verify with a password and are offered to create one. (No acr_values now means X.509 — the default — so passkey is requested explicitly.)

request.description:
Sends TWO space-separated acr_values: loa/low loa/high. the client policies route to the HIGHEST -> loa/high (2) = identity-first PASSKEY. No certificate needed, so this uses the plain-HTTP base. (Keycloak's built-in step-up would instead collapse to the minimum, loa/low = password.)

'Authorize using browser' ON. Log in as alice: enter username; if alice has no passkey yet you verify with the password and are offered to create one; acr=…/loa/high, amr=["hwk"] (or pwd while enrolling). Add …/loa/x509 to the Auth URL to make the highest become x509 (cert required) instead.

request.description:
Log in with a CLIENT CERTIFICATE over mutual TLS (:8443). X.509 is its own LoA level (acr_values=http://example.com/loa/x509, baked into the Auth URL); it requires a cert and has no password fallback.

Use 'Authorize using browser' = ON. Import certs/alice.p12 (password 'changeit') into your OS keychain / browser cert store first — the system browser presents alice's cert during the TLS handshake and Keycloak logs you in (amr=["x509"]).

NOTE: Postman's own 'Settings > Certificates' client certs are NOT presented on the OAuth authorize leg, so the non-browser mode can't do mutual TLS here. For a headless check use scripts/test_x509.py.

request.description:
Sends THREE space-separated acr_values: loa/low loa/high loa/x509. The native client policies (acr-condition + auth-flow-enforcer) route to the HIGHEST requested level -> loa/x509 (3), so this requires a client certificate over mutual TLS (:8443); acr=…/loa/x509, amr=["x509"]. (Keycloak's built-in step-up would instead collapse the list to the minimum, loa/low.)

Prereqs = same as the X.509 request: 'Authorize using browser' ON, import certs/alice.p12 (password 'changeit') into your OS keychain, and trust certs/ca.crt (or disable SSL verification). Drop loa/x509 from the Auth URL to see the highest become loa/high (passkey) instead.
